title: Compact 'stacked-cards' fallback for extremely narrow viewports in virtualized tables
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: On mobile and very narrow panels, our current virtualized table layout becomes unreadable (columns overflow, horizontal scroll is painful). Several product teams have requested a compact alternative view that preserves important row data and actions while staying efficient for large datasets.

Proposal: Introduce a fallback 'stacked-cards' density mode that automatically triggers below a configurable viewport width (e.g., 480px) or when all columns cannot reasonably fit. Each table row is rendered as a compact card containing: a prominent primary column header, 2–4 prioritized key-value fields, and a condensed actions overflow. Implementation must retain virtualization (large row counts) by using an estimated item-height strategy and an efficient measurement cache. The pattern should be opt-in per table (prop) and also available in the Console density dropdown as "Stacked" alongside Compact/Comfortable.

Goals: maintain sub-100ms perceived scroll latency for typical datasets, preserve keyboard-first navigation, keep SR-friendly semantics, and provide a smooth animated transition between grid and stacked modes. The feature should include accessible microcopy and ARIA-announce transitions so assistive tech users understand the layout change.
acceptance_criteria: Stacked mode renders each row as a compact card with primary header, up to four key-value fields, and actions overflow
Tables with stacked mode enabled should support virtualization for datasets of 50k rows without excessive memory usage (no more than 2x baseline DOM nodes compared to grid mode)
Estimated item-height measurement with cache must keep scroll jitter to < 8px on route changes and fast resizes
Keyboard navigation: Tab/Shift-Tab traverses expected interactive elements; Arrow keys move between logical rows; Enter opens actions; Space toggles expansion where present
Screen reader: switch to stacked mode triggers an aria-live polite announcement 'Table layout changed to stacked cards', and each card exposes proper role and relationships
Density control added to Console density dropdown with preview and persisted per-user preference
Unit and e2e tests covering transition animation, keyboard navigation, and virtualization edge cases
Design tokens used for spacing/typography and colors; no hardcoded pixel values in implementation
Performance regression baseline documented and reviewed in runtime-1.20 planning doc
comments: 2025-02-12 Ava Chen: Ticket created after discovery call with Product — engineering teams (ENG-19812) flagged mobile readability issues during customer alpha tests for Console query results.

2025-02-13 Marcus Patel: Initial feasibility review with Eng (runtime-team). Concern: virtualization relies on uniform row heights; stacked cards introduce variable heights. Proposed mitigation: use height estimator + background measurement task to warm cache for visible window.

2025-02-14 Sofia Reyes (Accessibility review): Recommend aria-live announcement on mode change and role=list/role=listitem semantics for cards. Suggest adding an opt-out data attribute for screen reader-only expanded metadata to avoid verbosity.

2025-02-17 Marcus Patel: Prototyped a CSS-only card layout in storybook. Basic virtualization works with heuristic estimator; measured initial scroll jitter ~12px for unpredictable content. Next: add measurement sampler and clamp max-card-height with overflow ellipsis for low-priority fields.

2025-02-18 Design review notes: reduce default key-value fields to 3 on mobile to improve density; provide primary column selector in table props (fallback to first visible column). Add microcopy for actions overflow: 'More actions' with aria-label.

2025-02-19 Engineering comment (ENG-19845): Created spike branch runtime/virtualization/stacked-cards. Memory regression across 100k items shows +18% peaks — acceptable with caching disabled during background sync. Will iterate on DOM reuse and virtualization buffer size.
2025-02-20 Ava Chen: Updated ticket with acceptance criteria and linked Figma prototypes. Scheduling handoff to Solutions Eng for customer validation in next cycle.
